claims.text: Heretical doctrine comes mainly from the Euagetaematikon, but each believer stresses different parts, from attacks on a Church said to serve Satan to Gnostic metaphysics.
Beneath it all lies one tenet every ghoul of the faith knows: the children of Caine are gods walking the earth.
In Heretical cosmology the false creator Ialdabaoth made Adam from mud, Sophia was both Lilith and Eve, Lilith bore Caine, and God marked Caine as a sign of favour after Abel’s death.
The mark is read as the gift of spirit within matter, so the Cainites hold the store of spirit for the whole world.
Counting from a creation date of 3761 B.C.E. and five stages of a thousand years each, Heretics expect the material world to end in 1239.
Then the Time of Gehenna comes, when the Blood of Caine thins and withdraws from the world, leaving it to crumble.
Most Heretics expect the Third Caine to appear in 1206 and dwell on earth for thirty-three years, like Christ.

title: Initiation into the Heresy
summary: How new members enter the faith.

claims.text: Some join by choice, through conversion or a corrupt bargain; others are made ghouls unawares by drinking wine laced with vitae.
Sects loyal to the Crimson Curia follow the Liturgy of Childeric exactly, while others borrow local pagan or Cathar forms or the fancies of a Toreador domitor.
Setite branches use cruel sexual initiation rites ending in a reward the novice craves.

title: Schismatics
summary: Heretical groups outside the main hierarchy.

claims.text: Many small groups grow beyond the reach of the Crimson Curia and its See of Nod, planted by human preachers, curious Toreador or rival clans.
The Heresiarchs tolerate them because souls are still bound to the Pleroma, and a purge might split the faith or reveal it to Rome.

title: Eschatologists of Cappadocius
summary: A Cappadocian faction devoted to the Heresy.

claims.text: These Graverobbers hold a more Christ-centred form of the Heresy and see themselves as the brood of both Caine and Christ.
They treat giving vitae to mortals as a sacrament, and the most fanatical call themselves the only true Christians.
They wander the back roads of Europe holding mass revivals.

title: Red Pentecost
summary: A Heretical rite of surrender to the Beast.

claims.text: In Red Pentecost, Heretics give themselves over wholly to the Beast and come back to their senses amid the slaughter they wrought.
Abbots, priors and knights alike are described waking bloodied beside victims they do not remember killing.

title: Recognising Heretical signs
summary: Rolls for spotting Heretical churches and symbols.

claims.text: Spotting a Heretical church from its decoration is a Perception + Theology roll, from difficulty 9 for a subtle shrine to 6 for a major Heretical centre.
Perception + Occult may spot Setite or Baali churches, which tend to be more blatant.
Heretics greet each other with signs and countersigns; an outsider who does not know them is very unlikely to notice anything, at difficulty 10.
